meta.note: Published slope limits and speeds of rovers, each with its source, for app/src/lib/route. slopeLimit is the limit used in operations or stated as the design requirement; otherSlopeFigures are shown for context. speed gives a lower bound on driving time. A rover with no published figure has null.
meta.energyNote: No published, simple, citable model of rover energy against slope was found. The only energy figure is the Apollo rover's measured rate on the Moon. Do not apply it to another vehicle, another body, or a slope.

slopeLimit.source: Rankin, Maimone, Biesiadecki, Patel, Levine and Toupet 2020, Driving Curiosity: Mars Rover Mobility Trends During the First Seven Years (JPL)
slopeLimit.note: 'the nominal flight tilt limit is 30 degrees. However, the tilt limit is typically lowered for each drive'. The largest tilt in the first seven years was 25.3 degrees.

speed.kind: maximum wheel speed (4.2 cm per second)
speed.source: NASA/JPL Robotics, Mars 2020 rover mobility page
speed.note: 'maximum wheel speed is just 4.2 cm/sec (or approximately 150 meters per hour)'.

otherSpeeds.kind: upper end of the rate when driving autonomously (15 to 18 m per hour)
otherSpeeds.source: NASA/JPL Robotics, Mars 2020 rover mobility page

slopeLimit.kind: slope above which a drive needs special planning
slopeLimit.source: Biesiadecki, Leger and Maimone 2007, International Journal of Robotics Research 26(1):91, doi:10.1177/0278364907073777
slopeLimit.note: 'driving on slopes greater than 25 degrees requires special planning'. The rovers drove on hard slopes of up to 31 degrees and are statically stable to 45.

slopeLimit.source: Bluethmann 2024, VIPER Rover Overview and Mobility and Hardware (NASA NTRS 20240013903)
slopeLimit.note: 'Slopes up to 15 deg (reqt)'. NASA's operations page adds that it can tackle 25 or 30 degrees when necessary.

otherSlopeFigures.kind: upper end of what it can tackle when necessary (25 or 30 degrees)

slopeLimit.source: Costes, Farmer and George 1972, Mobility Performance of the Lunar Roving Vehicle, NASA TR R-401 (NTRS 19730008090)
slopeLimit.note: The same report puts the wheel's climbing ability on simulated lunar soil at 18 to 23 degrees; the Apollo 17 crew found slopes of up to 20 degrees easy.

otherSlopeFigures.kind: slope the Apollo 17 crew negotiated easily, straight ahead

speed.kind: average speed while driving, Apollo 17 (the lowest of the three missions)
speed.source: Apollo Program Summary Report, JSC-09423, 1975, Table 4-IX and section 4.8 (NASA NTRS 19750013242)
speed.note: Mission averages were 9.2, 7.7 and 7.6 km per hour.

otherSpeeds.kind: average speed while driving, Apollo 15 (the highest)
otherSpeeds.source: Apollo Program Summary Report, JSC-09423, 1975, Table 4-IX and section 4.8 (NASA NTRS 19750013242)

energy.kind: measured mission rate, Apollo 16 (the highest of the three missions)
energy.source: Apollo Program Summary Report, JSC-09423, 1975, Table 4-IX and section 4.8 (NASA NTRS 19750013242)
energy.note: Derived: 2.1 ampere-hours per km x 36 volts. The three missions used 1.9, 2.1 and 1.64 ampere-hours per km. Measured on the Moon, at one sixth of Earth's gravity, for this vehicle with two astronauts. It is a mission average, not a function of slope.
